name: Personal Life System
description: One-person home essentials and short-disruption reserve. Initial plan: 14 days. Actual stock and unconfirmed supply start at zero. Rates are editable stock-use assumptions; fixed targets cover reusable equipment and contingency reserves. Complete meals include their ingredients. Configure personal medicines and glasses separately. Review quantities, expiry and equipment readiness regularly.

items.name: Emergency Water
items.note: Combined drinking, cooking and limited sanitation reserve. Do not count those uses again as separate stocks. Rounded storage-planning baseline, not a drinking prescription; adjust for climate and personal needs. Rotate by product guidance. Source: https://www.cdc.gov/water-emergency/about/how-to-create-and-store-an-emergency-water-supply.html

items.name: Food-grade Water Container (20 L)
items.note: 60 L capacity covers the initial 56 L plan. Empty containers are not water stock. Count existing bottled-water storage before buying more; increase capacity for longer intervals.

items.name: Reusable Water Bottle
items.note: Water inside is part of Emergency Water, not an additional reserve.

items.name: Water Treatment Device
items.note: Select for the actual water source and follow its instructions. Equipment alone does not guarantee potable water; unconfirmed supply remains zero.

items.name: Replacement Treatment Cartridge
items.note: Match the device; check rated capacity and replacement date. Fixed spare, not daily consumption.

items.name: Breakfast Meal
items.note: One complete breakfast meal per day from your own menu. Choose shelf-stable ready-to-eat options suitable for your dietary needs. A meal includes its staple, protein and produce components; count complete meal equivalents, not individual packages. This is a meal-count assumption, not a nutrition prescription. Rotate earliest expiry first.

items.name: Lunch Meal
items.note: One complete lunch meal per day from your own menu. Choose shelf-stable ready-to-eat options suitable for your dietary needs. A meal includes its staple, protein and produce components; count complete meal equivalents, not individual packages. This is a meal-count assumption, not a nutrition prescription. Rotate earliest expiry first.

items.name: Dinner Meal
items.note: One complete dinner meal per day from your own menu. Choose shelf-stable ready-to-eat options suitable for your dietary needs. A meal includes its staple, protein and produce components; count complete meal equivalents, not individual packages. This is a meal-count assumption, not a nutrition prescription. Rotate earliest expiry first.

items.name: Snack Portion
items.note: Optional daily allowance; adjust to your routine. Snacks do not replace complete meals.

items.name: Manual Can Opener
items.note: Set target to zero if your selected food packaging does not require it.

items.name: Bowl, Mug and Cutlery
items.note: One complete reusable personal eating set.

items.name: Lidded Cooking Pot
items.note: Normal household equipment. The outage meal plan should also work without powered cooking.

items.name: Kitchen Knife and Cutting Board
items.note: One food-preparation set.

items.name: Food Storage Containers
items.note: Daily food rotation; observe storage requirements for the actual contents.

items.name: Dishwashing Liquid
items.note: Editable usage estimate. Calibrate against one week of actual use and product dilution instructions.

items.name: Dishwashing Sponge
items.note: One in use and one spare; replace according to condition.

items.name: Soap
items.note: Editable stock-depletion estimate; calibrate to your product and routine.

items.name: Toothpaste
items.note: Inventory estimate, not an application dose. Adjust using actual tube consumption.

items.name: Toothbrush
items.note: One in use and one spare.

items.name: Towel
items.note: One in use and one available while washing or drying.

items.name: Toilet Paper
items.note: Example weekly use. Roll sizes differ; use a consistent product size or adjust the rate.

items.name: Waste Bag
items.note: Editable daily allowance; adjust to actual waste volume and collection interruptions.

items.name: Laundry Detergent
items.note: Example weekly stock use. Replace with actual product dose and washing frequency.

items.name: Hand Sanitizer
items.note: One labeled retail bottle as a reserve; follow its label.

items.name: Personal Care Supplies
items.note: Customize for menstrual products, shaving, continence or other needs. Split into individual material rows when usage is known.

items.name: Temporary Toilet and Liners
items.note: One kit appropriate to the home and local waste-disposal arrangements. Count the complete kit, including its liner reserve.

items.name: Adhesive Dressings
items.note: Fixed reserve, not a treatment schedule. Check packaging and expiry.

items.name: Sterile Gauze Pads
items.note: Fixed reserve; keep sealed until needed.

items.name: Medical Tape
items.note: Fixed personal first-aid reserve.

items.name: Elastic Bandage
items.note: Fixed reserve; use according to product instructions.

items.name: Nitrile Gloves
items.note: Count pairs, choose a suitable size, and replenish after actual use.

items.name: Protective Masks
items.note: Choose protection suitable for the actual exposure; follow replacement instructions.

items.name: Digital Thermometer
items.note: Check battery and keep operating instructions.

items.name: First-aid Scissors and Tweezers
items.note: Basic tools; this catalog does not assume invasive procedures.

items.name: Personal Prescription Medicines
items.note: Personal configuration required. Add each actually prescribed medicine separately, with the correct package unit and a reserve agreed with your clinician or pharmacist. No dose or need is inferred from duration.

items.name: Personal Nonprescription Medicines
items.note: Personal configuration required. Add only products suitable for you, following their labels. No default purchase target.

items.name: Medication and Allergy List
items.note: An accessible paper copy with medicines, allergies and care contacts. Count the copy; keep its sensitive contents outside shared inventory exports.

items.name: Sleeping Surface and Bedding
items.note: One complete personal setup; existing household equipment counts.

items.name: Warm Blanket or Sleeping Bag
items.note: Choose for the local temperature range and personal needs.

items.name: Emergency Blanket
items.note: Compact backup, not a replacement for suitable bedding or shelter.

items.name: Weatherproof Outer Layer
items.note: Rain and wind protection adapted to the climate.

items.name: Insulating Layer
items.note: Warm layer adapted to the climate.

items.name: Everyday Clothing
items.note: Three changes with a washing rotation; fixed equipment, not new clothing every day.

items.name: Underwear
items.note: Rotation assumption; increase if washing is unavailable.

items.name: Socks
items.note: Rotation assumption; increase if washing is unavailable.

items.name: Walking Shoes
items.note: One usable, well-fitting pair.

items.name: Spare Prescription Glasses
items.note: Configure only if relevant to your needs.

items.name: Usable Stored Electricity
items.note: Example budget for essential small electronics only, excluding cooking, heating, refrigeration and medical devices. Set stock to usable stored energy after losses. Device counts below are not extra energy. Replace this rate with a measured device budget; no grid or solar supply is assumed.

items.name: USB Power Bank
items.note: One in use and one backup. Record their combined usable energy in Usable Stored Electricity; this row counts devices only.

items.name: USB Charger
items.note: Match device requirements and available power sources.

items.name: Charging Cable
items.note: Two compatible, tested cables.

items.name: Headlamp
items.note: Hands-free lighting; include its consumption in the energy budget.

items.name: LED Lantern
items.note: Shared-space lighting; include its consumption in the energy budget.

items.name: Spare Device Batteries
items.note: One set is a complete replacement for a specified device. Split incompatible sizes into separate rows.

items.name: Mobile Phone
items.note: Keep emergency contacts and offline maps available.

items.name: Battery or Hand-crank Radio
items.note: Choose for local broadcasts and test power and reception.

items.name: Offline Maps and Contact List
items.note: Offline set with a paper fallback, meeting points and essential contacts.

items.name: Notebook and Pen
items.note: For plans, messages and manual records during outages.

items.name: Document Copies
items.note: Essential copies stored securely. Count the set; do not store document numbers or scans here.

items.name: Emergency Cash Reserve
items.note: One personally defined reserve. Choose its amount and denominations yourself; the count is not a currency amount.

items.name: Spare Keys
items.note: One spare set stored securely.

items.name: Emergency Backpack
items.note: Carries a portable subset. This warehouse is a home reserve, not a claim that all 14-day supplies fit in one bag.

items.name: Whistle
items.note: Non-powered signaling tool.

items.name: Work Gloves
items.note: For handling and cleanup; distinct from disposable first-aid gloves.

items.name: Multitool
items.note: Tools you can use safely and legally.

items.name: Repair Tape
items.note: General-purpose repair reserve.

items.name: Utility Cord
items.note: Ordinary fastening and repairs; not for climbing or life-safety loads.

items.name: Sewing Kit
items.note: Basic clothing repairs.

items.name: Smoke Alarm
items.note: Baseline count only. Actual number and placement must suit the dwelling and local guidance. Test as directed.

items.name: Carbon Monoxide Alarm
items.note: Check suitability, local requirements, placement and device operation.

items.name: Fire Extinguisher
items.note: Choose a suitable household product; check service status and accessible placement.
